messages:
maria: heads-up — noticed a new freeze on /dashboards when you hover over stacked-area charts. main thread blocks ~2-3s, charts stop responding. saw this on canary and prod.
jonathan: repro steps? browser / OS? trace?
maria: chrome 118 on mac, steps: open dashboard > wait for tiles > hover on series legend or datapoint. easy repro on large datasets. attaching console stack excerpt:

maria: ```
Long main thread task: parsing bundle (45ms) -> telemetry.flushSync() -> chart hover handler -> paint
// looks like telemetry flush is synchronous on hover
```
deploy-bot: FYI deploy 2026-03-18T09:12:02 -> frontend: bumped @chartlib/core 6.0.1 and telemetry-js 2.3.0 to canary.
sasha: interesting — telemetry-js 2.3.0 added a new opt-in "interaction flush" that does a sync XHR for immediate delivery when sample=true. we enabled interaction sampling in the rollout config last week.
kevin: if telemetry.flushSync is the culprit, can we gate it behind requestIdleCallback or debounce? Hover events are noisy.
anna: agree — two orthogonal problems: (1) chartlib 6.0.1 increased bundle size (parse + eval spikes) and exports a new hover plugin that wires into our telemetry by default; (2) telemetry change does sync flush on first interaction. combined, they make hover expensive.
jonathan: can we quickfix by disabling the plugin via chart init config? something like `plugins: { hoverPerf: false }` at runtime until we patch.
sasha: yes, setting hover plugin off should be quick. also change telemetry rollout flag back to sample=false for interaction events.
maria: i can try plugin-off in a canary patch. if that works, will push to prod rollback.
kevin: longer term: lazy-load chartlib hover plugin and move telemetry.instrument('hover') to a debounced queue + background flush. also add a budgeted sync path only for explicit actions (save/export) not hover.
anna: owner proposal: maria will push canary with plugin disabled + telemetry flag rollback. kevin will follow up with code for debounced telemetry queue. sasha will prepare a telemetry config change and a postmortem note for the rollout.
dev-bot: canary build created: frontend/canary/1749812351 (maria) — routed to 10% EU.
maria: confirmed canary shows immediate reduction in freeze (hover now ~30-60ms). rolling to 100% after 10m smoke. thanks all :thumbsup:
jonathan: add a charting regression test (hover interaction perf) to the dashboard CI? we should catch this earlier.
kevin: filing GH issue for debounced telemetry + lazy plugin import. i'll link to the canary perf numbers.
anna: note for release documentation: call out telemetry interaction sampling as a risky opt-in; we should default to async flush.
maria: will post follow-up with flamegraphs and CI test PR. closing thread once rollout is complete.
